newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to stress need to fix budget deficit at G7.
newsitem.headline: Japan to stress need to fix budget deficit at G7.

text.p: Japan plans to tell other Group of Seven (G7) leading industrial nations that its economy is recovering gradually and that staunching the red ink in its budget is vital, a Finance Ministry official said on Thursday.
"I think we hope we will be able to present that the Japanese economy is on a gradual recovery path," he said.
The official was speaking before International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank and G7 finance ministers' meetings in Washington later this month.
"I think that the minister (Finance Minister Wataru Kubo) will stress the urgent need" for fiscal consolidation, he said.
U.S. officials have repeatedly expressed the desire to see Japan take the necessary fiscal and monetary steps to keep its recovery on track.

There have also been some signs that politicians, now gearing up for an election expected in October, would like to see further stimulus in the form of an extra budget for the current fiscal year to March 1997.
But the Finance Ministry, worried about Japan's bulging budget deficit, has been cool towards the idea.

Japan enjoyed budget surpluses until 1992, but the balance has plunged into the red as the five-year slump and dwindling tax revenues forced the issuance of government bonds to finance stimulative packages.
In gross terms, Japan's total indebtedness is now nearly 90 percent of output, and appears headed for 100 percent. This compares with an average of just under 74 percent for OECD nations.
